I just pushed a commit to a branch of FLT on the command line rather than using VSCode, and was surprised to see this:

buzzard@IC-HWDXTW69VR FLT % git push
Enumerating objects: 5, done.
Counting objects: 100% (5/5), done.
Delta compression using up to 14 threads
Compressing objects: 100% (3/3), done.
Writing objects: 100% (3/3), 1.31 KiB | 1.31 MiB/s, done.
Total 3 (delta 2), reused 0 (delta 0)
remote: Resolving deltas: 100% (2/2), completed with 2 local objects.
remote:
remote: GitHub found 4 vulnerabilities on ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT's default branch (4 moderate). To find out more, visit:
remote:      https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT/security/dependabot
remote:
To https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT.git
   7629b6e..767cbd3  kbuzzard-module -> kbuzzard-module
buzzard@IC-HWDXTW69VR FLT %

Apparently I've had vulnerabilities for months. The link https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT/security/dependabot tells me I have four, all in my Gemfile.lock file. I am surprised that a file with a name like that contains any data at all (the lockfiles I've seen in the past have just been files which mean "don't edit this other file, something else is editing it" but apparently things have moved on. Apparently the FLT project has an XSS vulnerability and a DoS vulnerability, as well as some more exotic vulnerabilities. Should I be doing anything with this lockfile? I don't even know the purpose of the lockfile.

This is security noise, none of it will be anything relevant, it will have to do with irrelevant vulnerabilities in dependencies used when building FLT's docs site.

In the context of packaging, a lockfile is like lake-manifest.json -- it's the thing that says "not only do I depend on Mathlib, I depend on version XYZ of it, and it depends on version ABC of ProofWidgets at that time".

Here the Gemfile.lock is one for the versions of the ruby packages used to build your blueprint/docs site.

You are almost certainly safe to completely ignore that, and no one can see that number in the public view of the FLT repo as setup today.

But someone, possibly me once I've had coffee, will also regardless send you the tiny trivial PR to make the number go away. (I think if someone says PR twice Pietro appears right?? I should be careful)

These tend to be of the shape "you are transitively depending on a regular expression library. if you allow users of your website to use it to run arbitrary user-controlled regular expressions against arbitrary user-controlled text, your server may run out of memory"
(Sometimes they're more serious, but this kind of noise is typical in my experience)

In theory the dependabot PRs should solve this by submitting PRs to update your dependencies automatically, but there are still some issues with how docgen-action assumes a specific version of ruby which caused that to break things last time (#FLT > CI failure (blueprint ruby issue) )
